subject: Clarify: default retention, residency, and customer-initiated purge
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nexahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2025 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default and how we can purge

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Two quick follow-ups from our security team: can you confirm what Redwood keeps by default for a hosted deployment when we call the text-generation API? Specifically:  
- Are raw user inputs (prompts) stored by default, or only kept transiently?
- Are model outputs (generated responses) retained by default? If so, for how long and where do they live (US/EU regions)?
- What is the exact process for a customer-initiated purge: API, support ticket, or both? How do we get proof of deletion?

Also: does streaming behavior (partial tokens streamed during generation) change what is retained? Our compliance folks are trying to map retention windows for patient-identifiable info.

Appreciate any concise bullets or a short runbook — we need to include this in our vendor risk assessment.

Best,
Alex
Security Operations, NexaHealth

Attachment: nexarisk-questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexahealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2025 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default and how we can purge

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below is a short, operational summary and a short customer-facing runbook (high level). I attached a checklist your team can use.

Quick answers (hosted API, default settings):
- Prompts (user inputs): By default, we collect request payloads for 45 days to support ops/debugging and quality monitoring. These are stored in the region you select at account creation (US or EU). Default window: 45 days.
- Model outputs (generated responses): Also retained by default for 45 days; final outputs are indexed for search/quality but streaming fragments are kept only in transient buffers and not indexed unless the session completes and the output is persisted.
- Streaming tokens: transient stream buffers are ephemeral (kept in-memory or short-lived caches). If you use the streaming API and do not persist the final transcript via the SDK, intermediate tokens are not written to long-term storage.

Customer-initiated purge options (how to remove data sooner):
1) Self-service API: we offer a DELETE endpoint (/v1/customers/{id}/records) that accepts a request_date range and object types (prompts, responses, session_traces). Deletions initiated via the API are queued and processed; typical completion time is under 6 hours for small datasets (<100k records), up to 48 hours for larger archival purges.
2) Support/Compliance ticket: for audit-backed removal and deletion certification (PDF proof), open a ticket to compliance@redwood.com and include the data scope. We will run the purge and provide a signed deletion certificate and S3/Object-store purge logs where applicable.

Proof of deletion: we provide deletion manifests + cryptographic proof-of-erasure hashes for persistent stores and a signed certificate for SaaS customers. Note: audit logs that record the deletion event (who requested it, timestamp) are retained separately for 180 days for security auditing (these logs do not contain PII or content of prompts/outputs).

Exceptions and notes:
- Backups and disaster-recovery snapshots: backups are retained per our backup policy (up to 30 days). A deletion request that affects primary stores will also queue a retention-adjustment for backups; however, for legal holds or forensic copies there may be a short window (up to 72 hours) where data could persist while a BDR job completes.
- Private deployments (VPC / on-prem): retention is customer-configurable; Redwood can provide a default 0–45 day policy template but the customer controls enforcement.

Next steps: I attached our "customer purge checklist" (nexa-data-purge-checklist.pdf) and a short SLA excerpt for your review. If you'd like, we can walk through the API call structure on a short call tomorrow.

Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0121

Attachments: nexa-data-purge-checklist.pdf (pdf); signed-sla-excerpt.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@nexahealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2025 12:20:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Questions about what Redwood keeps by default and how we can purge

Adding a couple of clarifications from product/security standpoint:

- What "counts" as a stored artifact: final request payload (headers + body), final model output, and any derived embeddings or reranking artifacts are considered persisted artifacts. Session metadata (request IDs, routing metadata) is stored for observability and is scoped to 45 days by default.
- Streaming edge case: if a customer enables "persist_stream" in their tenant config, streaming fragments will be concatenated and treated as final outputs (and therefore retained). The default is persist_stream=false.
- Residency nuance: when customers choose "EU region", we store primary artifacts in EU locations. However, some ephemeral caches and cross-region routing metadata (small-sized, non-content) may transit or be stored in US telemetry stores for up to 7 days; we can add contractual covenants to restrict this for regulated customers.

Operational recommendation for NexaHealth:
1) Set tenant region to EU (if required by your data policy).
2) Keep persist_stream=false and use our final-output webhook to capture only final, accepted responses.
3) Use the DELETE API for routine purges and open a compliance ticket for certificate-backed erasure.

I'll ask Rishi to share a short example DELETE payload and retention-adjustment timeline snippet.

—Kimberly
Principal Product Security, Redwood
